# Azim Premji Philanthropic Initiatives Private Limited

<!-- Generated by `make client-docs`. Do not edit inside the markers. -->

Researched 2026-09-30 · status **partial** · Search and document budget largely spent; APPI's financial statements (Tofler/InstaFinancials/Zauba) are paywalled so no APPI-specific INR disbursement figure could be sourced, no INR grant-size range or grant amounts were disclosed anywhere found, and no dated RFP was found beyond the standing rolling-application process.

Azim Premji Philanthropic Initiatives (APPI) is a private grantmaking company (CIN U65999KA2000GAT026421, incorporated 2000, Bangalore) set up in 2014 as the grants arm of the Azim Premji Foundation — it is private philanthropy, not Section 135 CSR, and no evidence of section_135_bound status was found either way. It makes multi-year, largely unrestricted grants to Indian non-profits (12A/80G required, FCRA not required, 3+ years' track record preferred) working with marginalised groups across themes including gender justice, urban poor, disability, land & forest dependent groups, governance and civil-society strengthening, plus a flagship child-nutrition programme concentrated in Odisha. A confirmed 2024 grant partnership with the NGO Aarambh (child protection, Bagli block, Dewas district, Madhya Pradesh) was documented with no amount disclosed. Application is by concept note and invitation (not a fixed open call); a grant-registrations mailbox and a fraud-alert mailbox are published. No APPI-specific disbursement/spend figure in INR could be sourced (financial filings are paywalled); a Foundation-wide (not APPI-specific) figure of $109 million to 940 organisations in FY2023-24 appears in a TIME article but was not saved as an APPI figure due to entity ambiguity.

Website: https://azimpremjifoundation.org

## What it set out to find

- identity: legal name, parent/group relationship to Azim Premji Foundation/Wipro, website, entity type
- identifiers: CIN, domain
- csr_year/csr_spend: latest annual disbursement figures with FY (noting this is private philanthropy, not Section 135 CSR)
- programs/themes and geography where grants actually ran vs stated priority
- named grantee partners with amounts where disclosed
- how to apply: grant size, eligibility, process, open/rolling/invitation-only, contact
